newsitem.title: YEMEN: French archaeologists unearth 50 mummies in Yemen.
newsitem.headline: French archaeologists unearth 50 mummies in Yemen.

text.p: French archaeologists in Yemen have unearthed 50 mummies in excellent shape, the first such reported discovery in the country's modern history, an official said on Wednesday.

Abdul-Hamid Nouman Rajeh, governor of the northwestern area al-Muhweit, told Reuters the bodies were found in tombs built into rocks and "could reveal a lot of secrets about Yemeni life in distant decades and the people's way of life and thinking".
He gave no further details and said studies were needed to determine the age of the mummies, found in an area rich with untapped archaeological artifacts and riches.

French archaeologists were not immediately available for comment on the discovery in Yemen, a recent magnet for many Western tourists who flock to enjoy its the virgin nature and ancient civilisations.
In classical times, the Yemen formed part of the south eastern area of Arabia Felix. Sheba, which lasted from 950 to 115 BC, was one of the best known kingdoms in that region.
Seventeen Western archaeological missions are currently excavating in various parts of Yemen, one the Arab world's poorest states.
Parliament recently passed a law to protect antiquities and archaeological sites.
